must_catch: An inelastic collision means a collision that changes kinetic energy.
must_allow: Apply momentum conservation to an inelastic collision.
Two bodies collide along one line.

entries.syllabus_sentence: apply the conservation of momentum in simple applications, including elastic and inelastic collisions between two bodies in one dimension (definitions of an elastic and inelastic collision are not required)
entries.interpretation: Definitions are not required; one-dimensional two-body momentum applications remain in scope. Do not ban the collision terms themselves.
entries.automation_limit: Heuristic screen plus human context review; a passing regex check does not certify complete scope compliance.

must_catch: For a nuclear energy source, write a nuclide equation for the fuel reaction.
must_allow: Write a decay equation for beta emission.
Explain an advantage of a nuclear energy source.
Balance a nuclear equation in radioactivity.

entries.syllabus_sentence: discuss radioactive isotopes as the source of nuclear energy, its conversion to electrical energy and the problems associated with this process (no nuclide formulas are required)
entries.interpretation: Requires energy-source context. Nuclear Physics decay equations remain required. A paragraph-level pattern cannot replace a contextual review of an entire energy section.

must_catch: Calculate the diverging lens image distance using the lens formula.
must_allow: A diverging lens corrects short sight.
Draw rays showing a diverging lens correcting short sight.
Construct an image formed by a converging lens.

entries.syllabus_sentence: describe short sight and long sight and describe the correction of these eye defects (diverging lenses are only mentioned at this stage)
entries.interpretation: Diverging lenses are limited to eye-defect correction. Lexical screen catches selected standalone depth excursions; human context review is required for other formulations.
